course_description: Advanced relational database engineering, 3NF and BCNF normalization, physical storage architectures, B+ tree indexing strategies, query execution optimization, ACID transaction guarantees, concurrency control, and NoSQL document databases.

course_outcomes.co_description: Design normalized relational schemas achieving 3NF and BCNF to eliminate data redundancies.
Analyze complex SQL queries, execution plans, and B-Tree indexing strategies to optimize query performance.
Evaluate transaction management protocols, ACID guarantees, and concurrency control locking mechanisms.
Implement NoSQL document databases and distributed data pipelines for unstructured enterprise data.
Architect an enterprise database system incorporating automated backups, replication, and role-based security.

weekly_schedule.topic: Relational Model Review, Relational Algebra, and DBMS Architecture

lesson_outcomes.description: Define relational algebra operators (select, project, join, union)
Configure enterprise DBMS instances and SQL query workbenches
Acknowledge the vital role of persistent storage in computing
Identify superclasses, subclasses, specialization, and generalization
Construct comprehensive EER diagrams for complex enterprise domains
Appreciate precise conceptual abstractions before physical schema design
Define functional dependencies, candidate keys, and transitive dependencies
Decompose unnormalized data tables into 1NF, 2NF, and 3NF
Value mathematical rigor in eliminating update anomalies

weekly_schedule.topic: Boyce-Codd Normal Form (BCNF) and Multi-Valued Dependencies (4NF)

lesson_outcomes.description: Differentiate 3NF from BCNF and identify multi-valued dependencies
Perform lossless-join and dependency-preserving BCNF decompositions
Demonstrate precision when assessing non-trivial functional constraints

weekly_schedule.topic: Advanced SQL: Window Functions, Common Table Expressions (CTEs), and Subqueries

lesson_outcomes.description: Explain window partitions, ranking functions, and recursive CTEs
Write multi-table SQL queries leveraging CTEs and analytical partitions
Display diligence in formatting readable, modular SQL scripts

weekly_schedule.topic: Preliminary Examination: EER Modeling and Advanced Normalization Exam

lesson_outcomes.description: Recall relational algebra equations and normalization theorems
Execute timed schema normalization and complex SQL query tasks
Exhibit academic integrity and professional composure under evaluation

weekly_schedule.topic: Storage Architecture: File Organization, Page Slots, and Buffer Pools

lesson_outcomes.description: Describe slotted page architectures, free space maps, and LRU eviction
Calculate disk I/O overheads across differing buffer cache allocations
Appreciate low-level hardware constraints in data storage

weekly_schedule.topic: Index Structures: B-Tree and B+ Tree Fundamentals and Mechanics

lesson_outcomes.description: Explain search key distributions, fan-out, and split/merge mechanics
Trace index lookups, range scans, and node insertions in B+ trees
Value algorithmic logarithmic efficiency in data access

weekly_schedule.topic: Query Processing: Parsing, Translation, and Relational Optimization

lesson_outcomes.description: Describe cost estimation formulas for sequential scans versus index scans
Generate and interpret EXPLAIN ANALYZE execution plans in SQL
Strive for optimal query execution efficiency

weekly_schedule.topic: Index Tuning Strategies: Clustered vs Non-Clustered and Covering Indexes

lesson_outcomes.description: Differentiate clustered primary indexes from secondary covering indexes
Create targeted composite indexes that eliminate table lookups
Demonstrate prudence in managing index write-penalty overheads

weekly_schedule.topic: Stored Procedures, User-Defined Functions, and Automated Triggers

lesson_outcomes.description: Explain PL/SQL block structures, cursor loops, and event triggers
Program database triggers enforcing automated auditing and data integrity
Commit to defensive validation at the database layer

weekly_schedule.topic: Midterm Examination: Query Tuning and Index Optimization Practical Exam

lesson_outcomes.description: Synthesize index architecture, execution plans, and PL/SQL triggers
Profile and optimize poorly performing queries under timed inspection
Demonstrate technical competence under formal assessment

weekly_schedule.topic: Transaction Processing: ACID Properties and Concurrency Anomalies

lesson_outcomes.description: Explain dirty reads, non-repeatable reads, phantom reads, and atomicity
Simulate concurrent transaction conflicts using multi-session terminals
Recognize the severe financial impact of transactional data corruption

weekly_schedule.topic: Concurrency Control: Two-Phase Locking (2PL), Deadlocks, and Isolation Levels

lesson_outcomes.description: Contrast Read Committed, Repeatable Read, and Serializable isolations
Resolve deadlock cycles using wait-for graphs and timeout configurations
Value data consistency over raw concurrent throughput

weekly_schedule.topic: Database Recovery Protocols: Write-Ahead Logging (WAL) and Checkpointing

lesson_outcomes.description: Describe the ARIES recovery algorithm (Analysis, Redo, Undo phases)
Trace WAL log sequences to recover consistent database states
Emphasize disaster preparedness and fault tolerance in systems

weekly_schedule.topic: NoSQL Document Databases: MongoDB Schema Design and Aggregation Pipelines

lesson_outcomes.description: Contrast relational table models with flexible BSON document collections
Write multi-stage aggregation pipelines for nested document filtering
Appreciate scalability trade-offs in distributed data models

weekly_schedule.topic: Database Security, Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), and Replication

lesson_outcomes.description: Outline column-level privileges, encryption at rest, and replica sets
Configure role-based access control and read-replica failovers
Practice constructive team coordination during enterprise setup

weekly_schedule.topic: Final Examination & Capstone Defense: Enterprise Database Architecture Showcase

lesson_outcomes.description: Synthesize normalization, index tuning, transaction recovery, and NoSQL
Present and defend an enterprise database solution before evaluators
Exemplify Perpetualite leadership and professional presentation ethics
